record.question: Notwithstanding anything contained in this Code— -any Chief Judicial Magistrate; -any Metropolitan Magistrate; -any Magistrate of the first class specially empowered in this behalf by the High Court, may, if he thinks fit, try in a summary way all or any of the following offences: (I) offences not punishable with death, imprisonment for life or imprisonment for a term exceeding two years; (II) theft, under section 379, section 380 or section 381 of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860), where the value of the property stolen does not exceed two hundred rupees; (III) receiving or retaining stolen property, under section 411 of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860), where the value of the property does not exceed two hundred rupees; (IV) assisting in the concealment or disposal of stolen property, under section 414 of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860) where the value of such property does not exceed two hundred rupees; (V) offences under sections 454 and 456 of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860);
